delete_domain_message: Are you sure you want to delete this domain?
saml_settings: Your SAML settings have been saved, please login from incognito window to confirm that it has been set up correctly

auth_domain.domain_tooltip: The email domain for users who should use SSO (e.g., `example.com` for users with `@example.com` emails)
auth_domain.saml_description: Configure SAML 2.0 Single Sign-On with your Identity Provider. Read the <1>docs</1> for more information.
auth_domain.saml_acs_url_tooltip: The SSO endpoint of the SAML identity provider. It can typically be found in the SingleSignOnService element in the SAML metadata of the identity provider.
auth_domain.saml_entity_id_tooltip: The entityID of the SAML identity provider. It can typically be found in the EntityID attribute of the EntityDescriptor element in the SAML metadata.
auth_domain.saml_certificate_tooltip: The certificate of the SAML identity provider. It can typically be found in the X509Certificate element in the SAML metadata.
auth_domain.skip_signing_tooltip: Whether to skip signing the SAML requests. For providers like JumpCloud, this should be enabled.
auth_domain.saml_callout: SAML won't be enabled unless you enter all the attributes above
auth_domain.oidc_description: Configure OpenID Connect Single Sign-On with your Identity Provider. Read the <1>docs</1> for more information.
auth_domain.issuer_url_tooltip: The URL identifier for the OIDC provider. For example: "https://accounts.google.com" or "https://login.salesforce.com".
auth_domain.issuer_alias_tooltip: Optional: Override the issuer URL from .well-known/openid-configuration for providers like Azure or Oracle IDCS.
auth_domain.client_id_tooltip: The application's client ID from your OIDC provider.
auth_domain.client_secret_tooltip: The application's client secret from your OIDC provider.
auth_domain.skip_email_verification_tooltip: Whether to skip email verification. Defaults to "false"
auth_domain.get_user_info_tooltip: Use the userinfo endpoint to get additional claims. Useful when providers return thin ID tokens.
auth_domain.oidc_callout: OIDC won't be enabled unless you enter all the attributes above
auth_domain.google_description: Enter OAuth 2.0 credentials obtained from the Google API Console below. Read the <1>docs</1> for more information.
auth_domain.google_client_id_tooltip: ClientID is the application's ID. For example, 292085223830.apps.googleusercontent.com.
auth_domain.google_callout: Google OAuth2 won't be enabled unless you enter all the attributes above
auth_domain.google_workspace_groups_desc: Enable group fetching to retrieve user groups from Google Workspace. Requires a Service Account with domain-wide delegation.
auth_domain.fetch_groups_tooltip: Enable fetching Google Workspace groups for the user. Requires service account configuration.
auth_domain.service_account_json_tooltip: The JSON content of the Google Service Account credentials file. Required for group fetching.
auth_domain.fetch_transitive_membership_tooltip: If enabled, recursively fetch groups that contain other groups (transitive membership).
auth_domain.allowed_groups_tooltip: Optional list of allowed groups. If configured, only users belonging to one of these groups will be allowed to login.
auth_domain.type_group_email: Type a group email and press Enter
auth_domain.attribute_mapping_desc: Configure how SAML assertion attributes from your Identity Provider map to SigNoz user attributes. Leave empty to use default values.
auth_domain.email_attribute_tooltip: The SAML attribute key that contains the user's email. Default: 'email'
auth_domain.name_attribute_tooltip: The SAML attribute key that contains the user's display name. Default: 'name'
auth_domain.groups_attribute_tooltip: The SAML attribute key that contains the user's group memberships. Used for role mapping. Default: 'groups'
auth_domain.role_attribute_tooltip: The SAML attribute key that contains the user's role directly from the IDP. Default: 'role'
auth_domain.claim_mapping_desc: Configure how claims from your Identity Provider map to SigNoz user attributes. Leave empty to use default values.
auth_domain.email_claim_tooltip: The claim key that contains the user's email address. Default: 'email'
auth_domain.name_claim_tooltip: The claim key that contains the user's display name. Default: 'name'
auth_domain.groups_claim_tooltip: The claim key that contains the user's group memberships. Used for role mapping. Default: 'groups'
auth_domain.role_claim_tooltip: The claim key that contains the user's role directly from the IDP. Default: 'role'
auth_domain.role_mapping_desc: Configure how user roles are determined from your Identity Provider. You can either use a direct role attribute or map IDP groups to SigNoz roles.
auth_domain.default_role_tooltip: The default role assigned to new SSO users if no other role mapping applies. Default: "signoz-viewer"
auth_domain.use_role_attribute_tooltip: If enabled, the role claim/attribute from the IDP will be used directly instead of group mappings. The role value must match a SigNoz role name (e.g. signoz-viewer, signoz-editor, signoz-admin, or a custom role).
auth_domain.group_mappings_desc: Map IDP group names to SigNoz roles. If a user belongs to multiple groups, the highest privilege role will be assigned.
auth_domain.domain_to_admin_email_desc: Map workspace domains to admin emails for service account impersonation. Use "*" as a wildcard for any domain.
